# Lenalidomide-refractory status

Definitions, variables, evidence and design decisions for the model's lenalidomide-refractory
covariates. This file is the single home for refractory facts: `technical_review.md` points here
rather than restating them, and the programme's `_notes.md` describes the subsystem in prose only.

Figures are from the **251128** data cut unless stated.

**Provenance warning, and it has already cost a figure.** Section 3 is regenerated by
`prep/refractory_diagnostics.do` - **which does not exist**: it is an untracked one-off in
`scratch/refractory/`, so section 3 cannot be reproduced on a new cut. Section 7's figures come from
untracked one-offs too. In July 2026 this stopped being hypothetical: section 1.2 carried a
maintenance-refractory rate computed from `MNT_Len`, a variable that had since been retired, and the
figure turned out to be unreproducible by any route on the current extraction. It was replaced rather
than corrected. Promoting a tracked diagnostic is an open todo; 7.6 records what working from
throwaway scripts has cost.

**Where the working lives.** `scratch/refractory/notes.md` and `scratch/maintenance/notes.md` carry
what was tried and rejected, the numbers behind each decision, and the hypotheses already killed.
This file holds conclusions; those hold the reasoning. Read them before re-diagnosing anything here.

---

## 1. Definitions

### 1.1 Progression, relapse and refractory are distinct

Following the IMWG consensus on uniform reporting (Rajkumar et al.):

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Progression (PD)** | A disease-state event: >=25% rise in M-protein from nadir, or new bone lesions. A measurement, independent of treatment. |
| **Relapse** | Previously treated myeloma that progresses and requires salvage therapy but does **not** meet refractory criteria. The patient remains drug-**sensitive**. |
| **Refractory** | Disease that is non-responsive while on primary or salvage therapy, **or progresses within 60 days of last therapy**. Defined relative to a **specific therapy**. |
| **Primary refractory** | Never achieved minimal response or better on any therapy. |
| **Relapsed-and-refractory** | Achieved >=MR previously, then progresses within 60 days of last therapy. |

**The 60-day clock is the arbiter.** Progression within 60 days of a therapy (or non-response on it)
is refractoriness; progression later is relapse, and the patient stays sensitive to that drug. This
distinction is what the whole subsystem turns on.

### 1.2 Lenalidomide-refractory

The general definition applied to lenalidomide: progression while on a lenalidomide-containing
regimen, and/or starting a subsequent non-lenalidomide line within 60 days of stopping it.

**Receiving lenalidomide is not the same as becoming refractory to it.** In this cut, of 2,386
patients whose L1 induction contained lenalidomide, only **13.3% were refractory to that induction**;
86.7% responded. Of **1,031** patients whose L1 maintenance regimen was lenalidomide (`MNR_L1 == 1`),
**19.1% were refractory to it**; the rest came off for another reason and relapsed later. A patient
who responds to lenalidomide induction, transplants, and relapses two years later off all
lenalidomide is **len-sensitive at relapse**, not refractory.

**Read 19.1% as a prevalence, not as a simulation target.** 47% of those patients were still ON
maintenance at the data cut and so could not yet have progressed on it, which depresses the figure.
Among the 545 whose maintenance had ENDED the rate is **36.0%**, and that is the comparison for a
model, which runs every patient to completion and has no still-on group. Even 36.0% is a lower bound:
a patient who stays on maintenance longer has more opportunity to progress while on it, not less, so
the settled figure will sit above it as follow-up matures.

*(An earlier version of this section reported 20.1% of 1,341 patients, from a denominator built on
`MNT_Len`. That variable is no longer emitted - it was exactly `MNT_Drug == 1` and both were dropped
as redundant - so the figure cannot be recomputed on the current extraction by any route. It is
retired rather than corrected. Rebuilt on `MNR_L1 == 1` by `scratch/refractory/mntrefr_reconcile.do`.)*

### 1.3 Dose context, captured structurally

The literature distinguishes progression on **treatment-dose** lenalidomide (25 mg, unambiguously
refractory) from progression on **maintenance-dose** lenalidomide (5 to 15 mg), which is frequently
regarded as len-**sensitive**. The MRDR dose field is unreliable, so we do not use it. Instead the
distinction is captured **structurally, by the form the drug sits in**:

- lenalidomide in `tbl_Chemotherapy` = a treatment line (induction, or continuous Rd) -> **treatment dose**
- lenalidomide in `tbl_MaintenanceTherapy` = maintenance context -> **maintenance dose**

This is why the two flags are kept separate rather than collapsed (see 4.1). Cam's registry routines
use no dose data either.

### 1.4 Progression: the model's hybrid definition

Refractoriness needs progression events with dates. The model uses the **union** of two sources:

1. **Review structured**: `DPMProgDisease`, `DPMClinicalRelapse` (and the misspelled `DPMClinicalRelaps`),
   `DPMRelapseFromComplRemission`, `HasDisProgSinceLastRev`, `ReviewBCRtoDate == 9`.
2. **Treatment record**: chemotherapy indication (progressive disease / relapse / primary-refractory),
   its free-text, PD best response, and PD cessation. Dates come from the next line's start, the
   therapy end date, or the BCR test date, whichever is earliest.

**Both arms are required.** Of 3,072 patients with any progression, **390 (12.7%) are captured only
by the treatment record** and have no Review progression filed at all. A Review-only definition
misses them. Conversely the treatment-record arm alone (Cam's `..._current` subroutine) is too narrow
on the Review side.

**Review free-text was dropped**: it contributed **zero unique events**. Every free-text progression
was already caught by a structured field.

Event counts: 5,109 Review-structured, 4,817 treatment-record, 9,926 total.

### 1.5 Refractory flag construction

A **chemotherapy line** is refractory if any of:
- best clinical response is SD or PD (`BCR` in {5, 6}), or
- it ceased for progressive disease (`ReasonForCessation_Recode == 5`), or
- the **next** line's indication is primary-refractory, or
- a progression event falls in the window `[line start, line end + 60d]`.

A **maintenance episode** is refractory if:
- it ceased for progressive disease (`ReasonCesationId == 5`), or
- a progression event falls in `[start, end + 60d]`.

**Maintenance end-date rule** (see 4.5): use the recorded end date; if missing but the patient has a
subsequent line, assume maintenance ran until the day before that line; otherwise fall back to the
start date.

## 2. Variables

Built by `prep/sub/MRDR/build_refractory.do` and merged into `MRDR Long` by `prep/data_extraction.do`.
Both of those files are git-ignored under the data-governance rule (they touch raw MRDR), so this
section is the specification of record.

**Per chemotherapy line** (keyed on `CID`):

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `refr_line` | The line is refractory (IMWG, per 1.5) |

**Per patient (maintenance)**:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `refr_len_mnt` | Refractory to lenalidomide maintenance (any episode) |
| `refr_len_mnt_date` | Start of the earliest refractory lenalidomide-maintenance episode |
| `refr_len_mnt_l1` | Refractory to the **L1** lenalidomide maintenance - the `LENREFR_MNT` outcome (4.4). Built from the event skeleton, **not** from `refr_len_mnt`; missing where maintenance has not ended |

**Carried forward, as at entry to each line** (the modelling covariates):

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `refr_len_tx_in` | Refractory to a lenalidomide **treatment** line, from strictly prior lines |
| `refr_len_mnt_in` | Refractory to lenalidomide **maintenance**, applying from the first line starting after that episode |

`refr_len_tx_in` is a cumulative-any over strictly prior lines, so it is **0 at L1 entry by
construction** and rises across lines. `refr_len_mnt_in` is line-resolved by date via
`refr_len_mnt_date`, floored at `Line >= 2` (maintenance never precedes L1).

**The `_in` suffix means at-line-entry, held constant within the line, and it is not cosmetic.**
The underlying quantities move at every row - `refr_len_tx_in`'s is a running cumulative-any and
`refr_len_mnt_in`'s is a test on `Date0`. Read at a line-*start* row either is correct, so a
regimen `mlogit` would be fine; but the OS equations `stset` **across** a line's span, and a
covariate that changed mid-span would be silently treated as time-varying. Evaluating at entry and
holding it removes that. It also keeps the at-entry **covariate** visibly distinct from the
per-patient **source fact** `refr_len_mnt`, which is otherwise the same words in the other order.
Caveat: `Line` is capped at 6 upstream, so L6-L9 share a group and hold the L6 entry value; 5
records that L5+ has no contrast anyway.

**Naming (revised August 2026).** The refractory variables are one family under a `refr_` prefix,
lower case throughout, with **scope carried by the suffix**:

| Shape | Scope | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `refr_line` | per chemotherapy line, any regimen | `refr_line` |
| `refr_len_mnt`, `refr_len_mnt_date` | per-patient source fact, lenalidomide maintenance | - |
| `refr_len_mnt_l1`, `refr_len_l1..l9` | line-resolved | - |
| `refr_len_tx_in`, `refr_len_mnt_in`, `refr_len_in` | at-line-entry covariate, held within the line | - |

The previous scheme used `Line*` / `MNT_*` / `LenRefr_*_in`, which spread one concept across three
prefixes and two cases, and made `MNT_LenRefr` and `LenRefr_Mnt_in` the same words in the other order.

**Case now marks the layer, not the concept.** Lower case is a data column; UPPER is a Mata object or
a global (`LENREFR_TX`, `LENREFR_MNT`, `LENREFR_regimens`, `LENREFR_pother`), and the engine keeps its
own `vLenRefr_in` / `mLenRefr_in` convention for Mata state. Equation names still lead with the line
(`L1_MND`) while data columns trail with it (`MND_L1`) - that is deliberate and unchanged.

Earlier drops: `MNT_Len`, which was exactly `MNT_Drug == 1`; and `MNT_Drug` itself, a patient-level
priority coding over **any** episode, superseded by `MNR_L1` - line-resolved, what the engine
simulates, and what the cost engine prices. Later-line maintenance would be `MNR_L2+` if ever
modelled (7.3).

**L1 maintenance duration** (per patient, for the cost fix in section 7):

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `MND_L1` | Maintenance duration delivered inside the billed L1 gap, **days**. The **benchmark** target (`L1_MND` itself is fitted on the skeleton's maintenance events, not on this column). 0 where `MNT == 1` but no episode falls in the gap |
| `MNR_L1` | L1 maintenance regimen (0 none/other, 1 len, 2 dara, 3 carf, 4 bort, 5 thal), from the first episode **inside the gap** |

`refr_len_mnt_l1` is likewise built in `data_extraction.do`, but from the **event skeleton** rather
than from `refr_len_mnt`: maintenance ends at the earlier of its recorded end (111) and the L2 start
(20), and the patient is refractory if L2 begins within 60 days of that. It is **missing** where
maintenance has not ended - undetermined, not negative - so `logit` drops those rows and no separate
`ended` flag is needed.

**Changed August 2026.** It previously line-resolved `refr_len_mnt` against the billed L1 gap. That
version was never what `LENREFR_MNT` was fitted on: `risk_equations.do` built its own skeleton
outcome at fit time and used that, leaving the extraction column with no consumer. The two disagree
substantially, so the skeleton version was moved into the extraction and the other retired
(`scratch/refractory/mntrefr_defcheck.log`):

| | |
|---|---|
| Skeleton definition, among the 545 whose maintenance ended | **28.6%** (156/545) |
| Old `refr_len_mnt_l1`, over all 1,031 rows | 18.9% |
| Disagreement on the 545 determined rows | 84 (15.4%) - **61** flagged by the old version only, **23** by the skeleton only |
| Of the 486 still on maintenance, old version flagged | **1** - the other 485 were coded 0 rather than missing |

The disagreement is **two-way**, so these are not nested definitions. The 61 are largely the
cessation-reason limb, which the engine cannot compute (4.4). The 23 are cases the skeleton reaches
through the L2 start date and the episode tables miss, consistent with the progression
under-recording that 1.5 already works around. Fitted on the same 544 rows, the skeleton outcome
gives pseudo R2 0.0615 / AUC 0.665 against 0.0527 / 0.658; on its own diluted sample the old version
falls to 0.0384 / 0.636.

Building it in the extraction also removes a bootstrap artefact: `risk_equations.do` derived it
*after* the bootstrap date shift, so the 60-day threshold was evaluated on nudged dates.

These are built in `data_extraction.do`, not `build_refractory.do`, because the billed gap
(`[DateL1E, gap end]`, gap end = L2 start, else death, else last follow-up) is a `MRDR Long` concept
rather than a raw-table one. `MND_L1` is the **overlap** of every episode with that gap, summed, so
that later-line maintenance is excluded and maintenance running past the gap is clamped (see 7.6).

`MNR_L1` is kept at six levels here even though `L1_MNR` fits it as a binary: the extraction records
what the registry says, and the pricing needs the regimen. The collapse is `risk_equations.do`'s job.

The event skeleton carries **no maintenance events** - the rows are still dropped, as they always
were. `L1_MND` and `L1_MNR` are fitted at the L1-end row rather than as survival equations on the
skeleton, so they need patient-level columns and nothing is restored. `MNT` and the skeleton are
unchanged: all of the above is additive.

`multiple_imputation.do` carries **six** of the above into `MRDR Long MI`: `MND_L1` (the benchmark
target) and `MNR_L1` for the maintenance equations - the `L1_MND` survival fit reads the maintenance
start/end EVENTS (110/111) kept in the skeleton, so it needs no duration or censoring column -
and `refr_line`, `refr_len_tx_in`, `refr_len_mnt_in` and `refr_len_mnt_l1` for the refractory ones - the
generation-model outcomes and covariates. `refr_len_mnt` and `refr_len_mnt_date` stop at `MRDR Long`,
having already been consumed by the extraction. That file's `keep` list is **explicit**, so anything
not named there is silently dropped, and until July 2026 that was the whole refractory family - which
is why none of it had ever reached an equation.

**Removed August 2026** as built-but-never-read: `MNT_TTM_L1` (the start offset the simple-first
duration model dropped), `MNT_Refr` (the any-drug flag, superseded by the lenalidomide-specific
chain), and `LineProg` / `LineProgDate` (`LineProgDate` fed only `LineProg`; neither feeds `refr_line`,
which comes from `refbase | inwin`). `refr_ep` is retained in `build_refractory.do`: it still builds
`refr_len_mnt`. Diagnostics under `scratch/refractory/` that read the removed columns
(`check_long.do`, `line_check.do`, the `mnd_tail*` family) need editing before they will re-run.

---

## 3. Evidence base

> **These figures predate the `_in` change (2, July 2026) and were fitted on the running variables,
> but none of them move.** Every section here reads the flags at a line-*entry* row, where the running
> value and the held value are identical by construction. 3.3 is worth spelling out because it looks
> like the exception and is not: `scratch/refractory/refractory_outcomes.do` snapshots the flags at
> `Event0 == 20`, collapses to one row per patient, and stsets OS from L2 as a plain baseline Cox -
> so its covariates are fixed at L2 entry and there is no span for a running value to change across.
> The `_in` variables exist for the equations that *do* `stset` over a line's span (the OS family in
> `risk_equations.do`), which is where a running covariate would silently become time-varying and
> start capturing "became refractory *on* this line" - the circularity 4.2 forbids.

### 3.1 Exposure and prevalence

- Chemotherapy lines: 11,752 in `MRDR Long`; **4,022 (34.2%) contain lenalidomide**; **45.3% of all
  lines are refractory**.
- Lenalidomide by line: L1 40.4%, L2 27.3%, L3 39.9%, L4 25.5%, L5 13.3%, L6 8.0%.
- Maintenance: 2,553 records / 2,102 patients. Drug mix: **lenalidomide 61.7%**, thalidomide 19.3%,
  bortezomib 8.9%, daratumumab 6.2%, carfilzomib 0.9%.
- Maintenance refractory 19.1% of records; lenalidomide-maintenance refractory 20.3%.

Exposure routes (patients with an L1 line, n = 5,906) and their len-refractory rates:

| Route | n | Any len-refractory |
|---|---|---|
| Len-naive | 2,913 | 0% (by definition) |
| L1 induction only | 1,658 | 17.8% |
| Maintenance only | 607 | 25.4% |
| Induction + maintenance | 728 | 18.7% |

The large len-naive group is real: lenalidomide was historically PBS-funded at second line in
Australia, so much of the registry received bortezomib-based L1.

### 3.2 Accrual across lines

Refractoriness accrues **throughout** the pathway, not only L1 to L2. Status as at line entry:

| Line entered | `refr_len_tx_in` | `refr_len_mnt_in` | Either |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | 0.0% | 0.0% | 0.1% |
| L2 | 8.7% | 8.9% | 16.0% |
| L3 | 27.3% | 9.6% | 35.4% |
| L4 | 57.6% | 10.2% | 65.8% |
| L5 | 71.3% | 10.9% | 78.5% |

**Incident** treatment refractoriness among those still at risk: L1 4.1%, L2 11.8%, **L3 24.0%**,
L4 17.5%, L5 10.1%. The largest single accrual is at **L3**, where lenalidomide is salvage into
already-progressing disease. Maintenance refractoriness is overwhelmingly a post-L1 event (incident
3.5% after L1, negligible later; onset at L2 for 82.9% of cases, L3+ for 15.4%).

### 3.3 Outcomes from L2

Among the 2,791 patients reaching L2:

| Group | n | Median OS |
|---|---|---|
| Not len-refractory | 2,304 | **54.0 mo** |
| Len-refractory (either) | 487 | **34.1 mo** |

Log-rank chi2(1) = 34.3, p < 0.0001. Landmark survival (not refractory vs refractory): 12 mo 87/76%,
24 mo 73/60%, 36 mo 62/47%, 60 mo 46/33%.

The effect is refractoriness, not exposure:

| Group | n | Median OS |
|---|---|---|
| Len-exposed, **sensitive** | 536 | **72.3 mo** |
| Len-naive | 1,768 | 48.8 mo |
| Len-**refractory** | 487 | 34.1 mo |

Exposed-but-sensitive patients do **best**. Refractory vs exposed-sensitive: chi2(1) = 68.6,
p < 0.0001. This is the strongest contrast in the analysis.

**The dose gradient** (the basis for keeping two flags):

| Group | n | Median OS |
|---|---|---|
| Not refractory | 2,304 | 54.0 mo |
| **Maintenance-dose** refractory | 244 | **47.2 mo** |
| **Treatment-dose** refractory | 243 | **24.7 mo** |

Age/R-ISS-adjusted Cox: either HR **1.53** (1.25 to 1.86); entered separately, `refr_len_tx_in` HR
**1.62** (1.25 to 2.11) and `refr_len_mnt_in` HR **1.34** (1.01 to 1.76).

Per-line OS with both flags together (adjusted for age and R-ISS):

| Line | `refr_len_tx_in` HR (p) | `refr_len_mnt_in` HR (p) |
|---|---|---|
| L2 | 1.62 (<0.001) | 1.38 (0.043) |
| L3 | 1.32 (0.006) | 1.61 (0.006) |
| L4 | 1.54 (0.001) | 2.46 (<0.001) |

Both flags retain independent signal at every line.

### 3.4 Regimen choice: the mechanism

Len-refractory status effectively bans Rd. L2 regimen (event year >= 2019):

| L2 regimen | not len-refr | maint-refr | treatment-refr |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Rd** (len-based) | 16.6% | **0.0%** | **1.3%** |
| **DVd** | 22.0% | 55.1% | 46.4% |
| other | 61.5% | 45.0% | 52.3% |

L3: Rd 32.7% / 0.9% / 3.8%; Kd 6.9% / 23.9% / 17.7%.

`mlogit` relative risk ratios (base = other): L2 Rd RRR 0.076 for `refr_len_tx_in` (p < 0.001) and
approximately 0 for `refr_len_mnt_in` (perfect avoidance); L2 DVd RRR 2.21 and 3.94 (both p < 0.001).
L3 Rd 0.078 / 0.027 (p < 0.001); L3 Kd 1.89 / 2.01 (p < 0.01). L4: `refr_len_tx_in` significant
(Kd 2.45, Pd 3.04, p ~ 0.001), `refr_len_mnt_in` not (p = 0.075 to 0.16).

A regimen equation carrying `Age Age2` only cannot reproduce this: it would keep prescribing Rd to
len-refractory patients, which never happens.

### 3.5 Predicting refractoriness (for the engine)

Synthetic cohorts carry no refractory status, so the engine must generate it.

**Treatment lines are partly definitional.** `build_refractory.do:136` sets `refbase = 1` if
`BCR in {5,6}`, so on the **registry** an SD/PD line is refractory with probability 1 and needs **no
equation**. That is the arm 4.4's engine rule stands on, and it is exact by construction.

| BCR | refractory: registry (observed BCR) | refractory: `MRDR Long MI` (imp 1) |
|---|---|---|
| CR | 23.3% | 21.8% |
| VGPR | 25.8% | 24.9% |
| PR | 41.7% | 37.3% |
| MR | 65.0% | 52.1% |
| **SD** | **100%** | **77.7%** |
| **PD** | **100%** | **82.4%** |

> **The definitional rule does not survive imputation. Anyone fitting or checking this arm on the MI
> data must know it.** `BCR` is `mi register imputed` (`multiple_imputation.do:134`); `refr_line` is
> not registered and is carried as observed. The imputation model does not know the two are
> deterministically linked, so it assigns SD/PD to rows the registry never flagged: **111 of 562
> SD/PD rows (19.75%) have `refr_line == 0`** on imputation 1. The registry definition is intact and
> the **engine is unaffected** (it simulates `BCR` and applies the rule, reproducing the registry
> join exactly). What is affected is the *data*: the MI file cannot be used to verify the
> definitional arm, and the residual arm's **membership** carries the same noise, since ~29% of its
> rows have an imputed `BCR`. A separate oddity from the same run: **173 len line-start rows still
> have `BCR` missing after `mi extract 1`**, which should not happen for a registered-imputed
> variable and is unexplained.
>
> That all 111 violators are imputed rows is **inference, not yet measured** - it follows from
> `refbase`, since an observed SD/PD cannot violate. `line_check.do` 2a tests it directly, but
> errored before reaching the test (see the Log entry for 17 Jul) and needs a re-run.

Only the residual arm (responders, BCR 1 to 4) needs a logit, and it is well predicted:

| Model (residual arm, `MRDR Long MI` imp 1, n = 3,283) | Pseudo R2 | AUC |
|---|---|---|
| No line term (baseline + BCR + prior state) | 0.078 | 0.675 |
| **+ line, L4+ collapsed** | **0.319** | **0.856** |
| + line at full resolution (`i.Line`) | 0.319 | 0.856 |
| Maintenance, baseline only | 0.042 | 0.639 |
| Maintenance, + SCT + BCR_L1 | 0.076 | 0.693 |

**Line is the model.** Odds vs L1 are ~13x at L2 (z = 23.0) and ~23x at L3 (z = 21.8). Everything
else is a tilt on top of it. Also predictive: the **BCR gradient** (PR 0.57, MR 0.69, both
p < 0.001; VGPR n.s.), **ECOGcc** (p = 0.015 and 0.041) and **prior refractory state**
(`refr_len_tx_in`, 0.75, p = 0.012).

Age, sex, all four comorbidity flags **and R-ISS** are non-significant. The line term is `i.Line`,
not a rebuilt `Event0/10` counter: the two agree perfectly below the cap at 6, so the counter that
`refractory_predict.do` built for itself was drift. Full resolution buys **nothing** over the
collapse (identical AUC, LR chi2(2) = 0.04, p = 0.982), and `keep if Line <= 4` is strictly worse
than collapsing: it drops 47 of 3,287 rows (1.43%, 80.9% refractory) while the engine applies one
coefficient at L4+ either way.

**Two covariates are line in disguise.** Drop the line term and `refr_len_tx_in` inflates from 0.75
to 2.56 (z = 9.13); in the earlier complete-case fit `ECOGcc` did the same thing. Later-line
patients are sicker and already refractory, so both proxy for line until line is there to absorb
them. Neither coefficient should be read causally.

> **Provenance, and a warning that generalises.** These figures come from `line_check.do` on
> `MRDR Long MI`. They supersede an earlier set from `refractory_predict.do`, which read
> `MRDR Long` and so fitted **n = 952 of a 2,335-row residual arm**: listwise deletion on 41% of
> the data, mostly via `BCR`. Imputing it more than triples the sample, and **three covariate calls
> reverse**: `ECOGcc` 0.118/0.075 -> 0.015/0.041 (n.s. to real), `R-ISS 3` 0.007 -> 0.774 (real to
> n.s.), `refr_len_tx_in` 0.288 -> 0.012 (n.s. to real). The AUC also falls, 0.892 -> 0.856, on 3.5x
> the data. An earlier draft of this section quoted the deleted fit and, worse, mixed a p-value
> from the baseline-only model into a sentence of adjusted figures. Hence the rule the
> specification now follows: **carry the pre-specified baseline set regardless of significance.**
> Selecting on in-sample p-values biases the survivors away from zero, and here it would have
> dropped two real covariates and kept one that is not there. `CLAUDE.md` is explicit that the
> out-of-sample validation is the arbiter, not in-sample fit.

**Maintenance refractoriness is barely predictable *by a logit on baseline covariates*** (AUC 0.69
here, and 0.586 when re-measured like-for-like in 4.4). The definitional tail rule 4.4 proposed as a
replacement is withdrawn; the shipped generation model is this logit, `LENREFR_MNT`, drawn once per
patient at L1E. It assigns roughly the marginal rate with a mild covariate tilt, which is an honest
outcome rather than a defect, but the coefficients should not be over-interpreted.

**Refitted August 2026 on the rebuilt MI data, the model is weaker still: `Prob > F = 0.073`, and the
response term is non-significant** (`bcr_grp_l1` 0.19 and 0.42, both n.s.), against the monotone
+0.66 / +1.14 / +1.17 and AUC 0.708 previously recorded here. The outcome is unchanged - the
definition check reproduces 156/545 exactly - so the difference is in the covariates, and the most
likely cause is the per-line rebuild of the `BCR_L1` imputation, which moved the L1-to-L2 association
by a third to a half. The response term is **retained regardless of significance**, per the
pre-specified-baseline rule above. Treat the specification argument earlier in this section - that
`i.BCR_L1` beat the alternatives on AIC and AUC - as measured on the superseded imputation.

---

## 4. Design decisions and rejected approaches

The reasoning a reviewer will challenge.

### 4.1 The two flags are kept separate, not collapsed

Treatment-dose refractoriness is severe (median OS 24.7 mo, HR 1.62); maintenance-dose is mild
(47.2 mo, HR 1.34) and sits much closer to non-refractory (54.0 mo). Collapsing them would hide a
22-month median-OS gap between two groups that are clinically different, and they capture largely
different patients (overlap at L2 entry is only 48 of 487). This also lets the lenient (Cam-consistent)
and strict (treatment-dose only) definitions both be tested without rebuilding.

### 4.2 TFI_L1 gets no refractory flags: circularity

Len-refractory status is **defined by** the progression event that closes the interval into the next
line. `refr_len_mnt_in` means "progressed on/within 60 days of L1 maintenance", and that progression is
what **starts L2**, i.e. what **ends TFI_L1**. Regressing TFI_L1 on it is close to tautological.

The data make the point unmistakably. Median TFI_L1: **3.9 months** for not-maintenance-refractory
patients vs **22.0 months** for maintenance-refractory. The refractory group looks five times
**better**, because to be maintenance-refractory you must have had maintenance, and maintenance takes
about two years. The association is an artefact and points the wrong way.

`refr_len_tx_in` is likewise endogenous to TFI_L1 and redundant with `BCR_L1` / `BCR_SCT`, which are
already in that equation. **Neither flag enters TFI_L1 or DN_TFI.**

The general rule: status as at a line's entry may predict that line's regimen, response, survival and
outgoing interval, but never the interval that **defined** it.

### 4.3 TXD and response are excluded: no independent signal

Fitting the model's actual specifications **plus** the flags:

| | `refr_len_tx_in` | `refr_len_mnt_in` |
|---|---|---|
| L2 TXD | HR 1.15, p = 0.31 | HR 0.89, p = 0.46 |
| L3 TXD | HR 1.15, p = 0.29 | HR 1.22, p = 0.33 |
| L2 TFI | -0.71, p = 0.063 | **-1.21, p = 0.003** |
| L3 TFI | -0.33, p = 0.24 | -0.01, p = 0.97 |

Refractoriness adds **nothing** to treatment duration once `BCR` and `TXR` are present: duration is
driven by how well the line works (`BCR_L2` HR up to 4.88 for PD) and which regimen (Rd HR 0.55,
continuous therapy). Its effect on duration flows **through** the response and regimen it selects.

Response (`ologit BCR`) is likewise non-significant after adjustment (L2 p = 0.098 and 0.34;
L3 p > 0.4).

The single exception is `refr_len_mnt_in` in TFI_L2 (p = 0.003). It is deliberately **not** included in
the first specification, on grounds of parsimony and to keep the engine change to `sim_txr` and
`sim_os` only. It is a flagged candidate: if the out-of-sample validation shows the L2 to L3 timing
is off, this is the first refinement to try.

### 4.4 Both generation models are definitional, not free logits

A free-standing logit on baseline characteristics would let the engine produce contradictory states
(a simulated CR patient flagged refractory, a PD patient flagged sensitive), because BCR in {5,6}
**is** part of the definition. The engine therefore does:

```
if the line contains lenalidomide:
    if BCR in {SD, PD}  ->  refractory                      (definitional, no equation)
    else                ->  Bernoulli(p), p from the residual logit (the 60-day arm)
```

**The tail rule was proposed here and is withdrawn; a fitted logit ships in its place** (`LENREFR_MNT`,
3.5, drawn once per patient at L1E from CRN slot 78). The rest of this section is the evidence for
the withdrawal and is kept because the rule is an obvious thing to re-propose. 1.5 makes
an episode refractory if it ceased for progressive disease, **or** if a progression event falls in
`[start, end + 60d]`. The progression that ends the L1 gap *is* the L2 start, so once the engine
knows when maintenance started and how long it ran, that second limb reduces to arithmetic:

```
tail = TFI_L1 - TTM - MND_L1                (maintenance end -> L2 start)
refr_len_mnt_l1 = 1  if  tail <= 60 days
```

This section previously specified that rule at **AUC 0.905** against the 3.5 logit's 0.69. **Both
figures were wrong and the rule does not work.** The score that earned 0.905 also contained
`rcess == 5`, cessation for progressive disease, which is 1.5's FIRST limb. Three things follow, any
one of them fatal: it is close to a restatement of the outcome, since `build_refractory.do` derives
the flag from progression events and "ceased for progressive disease" is the same clinical fact in a
different column; the comparison was not like-for-like, because the logit never saw that column; and
**the engine cannot compute it at all**, because reason-for-cessation is not modelled anywhere in the
pathway. 76.9% was never a rate the engine could reach.

Re-measured on the same 230 lenalidomide patients with a complete gap (`scratch/refractory/mnd_tail3.do`,
`mnd_tail4.do`):

| score | AUC |
|---|---|
| `rcess == 5` alone, no tail at all | 0.880 |
| tail alone, drawn - what the engine implemented | 0.637 |
| tail OR `rcess` - what this section reported as 0.905 | 0.912 |
| the 3.5 / 4.4 logit, baseline covariates | 0.586 |
| baseline + `ln(TFI_L1)` | 0.682 |
| baseline + `ln(TFI_L1)` + the tail as a CONTINUOUS predictor | 0.800 |
| baseline + `ln(TFI_L1)`, fitted AT RISK with censoring, no tail covariate | 0.801 |

The last row is `scratch/maintenance/mnd_tailmodel2.do` (22 July 2026) and is the best-founded of
these, though **not** better discriminating: it matches the 0.800 row without needing the tail as a
covariate, which matters because the tail is a derived quantity the engine must construct from a
drawn `MND`. It is fitted on the population genuinely AT RISK for a tail - maintenance ended, then
either observed reaching L2 or right-censored still in the gap - rather than on complete gaps. That
excludes the **725 of 1,570** patients still on maintenance at the cut, who have no tail yet and
whose inclusion as zero-length tails is what made an earlier cut of this diagnostic unusable. Note
this does NOT address the composition defect in 5(6): a better-specified logit does not fix a
generation mix that produces maintenance-refractory patients six years too young at three times the
treatment-refractory rate. That was the reason the arm was held until the mix defects were fixed (4.7).

The deeper failure is not the draw and not the contamination. On **observed** MND, with no draw and
no `rcess`, the rule under-calls in every gap band and the error widens as the gap grows, because the
median tail walks from 0.67 to 4.65 months straight past the 1.97-month threshold:

| gap band | median tail | registry | tail rule says |
|---|---|---|---|
| <12mo | 0.67 mo | 83.3% | 75.0% |
| 12-24mo | 1.26 mo | 79.0% | 59.3% |
| 24-42mo | 3.16 mo | 60.0% | 41.1% |
| 42mo+ | 4.65 mo | 56.8% | 37.8% |

The engine placed half its lenalidomide maintenance patients in band 4 and reported **33.7%** against
a registry 70.4%. That is the band-4 row, faithfully implemented. There was no coding defect to find;
the rule is simply wrong at the gap lengths the model runs at. `mnd_tail.do`'s "85.9% agreement" was
pooled on a sample where short gaps dominate.

Not the mechanism: the `share = 1` boundary mass that a Beta cannot represent is **2 patients in
589**. Registry maintenance ends about 28 days *before* L2 rather than at it, so the shares crowd
near 1 without reaching it. One-inflation is out.

**The binding constraint was selection, not functional form - and it is what drove the redesign.** A
*share* needs an observed gap END, so the withdrawn `betareg` share and every rule built on it were
fitted on complete gaps only, median **23.9 months**. The population they are applied to has a true
median far longer: the registry's own KM puts ASCT/CR patients at a median TFI of **73.5 months**, P75
142.8 (`tfi_l1_asct.csv`). The DURATION has since escaped this: `L1_MND` no longer carries a gap
covariate, so it fits on the whole maintenance population and the ordering is enforced by the
truncated `TFI` draw instead (7.4). **A refractory rule computed from the tail has not escaped it**,
because a tail still needs an observed L2 to be complete - 505 of 1,031 lenalidomide maintenance
patients have no recorded maintenance end at all, consistent with the ~43% of maintenance records
lacking an end date. So the constraint that was retired for the duration still binds on any
tail-based refractory rule, and that is a reason to prefer a fitted logit over a rule.

So the engine ships **without** a maintenance refractory generation model. Paths forward, in the
order they should be tried:

1. **Model maintenance DURATION on the maintenance events, gap-dependent via ln(TFI_L1).** `streg`,
   including those still on maintenance and those who never reach L2, which is precisely the
   selection a share cannot escape. `mtd_streg.do` found 42.5% of predicted durations exceeding the
   gap, which is why an earlier version moved to a share; but capping the draw at TFI turns that
   overshoot into continuous-to-progression maintenance rather than an error. **This was built for
   the cost model (7.4): a capped `streg` duration.** The refractory flag is the same capped
   duration reaching (within 60 days of) the relapse - derivable, not yet wired in.
2. **The continuous tail in a logit** (0.800 above, against a 0.880 ceiling set by a column the
   engine does not have). It must be re-measured with the DRAWN tail rather than the observed one:
   the draw cost the hard rule 0.08 AUC, so its honest figure is lower.
3. **Concede that it is not predictable and assign at the marginal rate.** The baseline logit is
   0.586 with LR chi2 p = 0.30 and pseudo R2 0.013, i.e. an intercept-only model wearing covariates.
   If 1 and 2 fail this is the honest answer, and it at least reproduces the population rate, which
   is what gates later-line eligibility.

**Two traps, both of which caught this section, both worth stating as rules.** *Test with what the
engine will have.* Every wrong number above came from a test that used something unavailable at
simulation time: first `fracreg`'s conditional mean where the engine draws, then `rcess` which the
engine cannot compute. And *check what went into the score before reading the score*: the 0.905 was
reproduced exactly (0.912) once `rcess` was put back, which is how the contamination was confirmed
rather than argued about.


### 4.5 Maintenance end-date rule

42.9% of maintenance records have no end date, and **all** of them also lack a cessation reason. But
**92.6% of those have no subsequent line**: they are **ongoing maintenance** at the data cut,
correctly not refractory, and the start-date fallback does them no harm. Only **81 records (7.4% of
missing-end, 3.2% of all)** have a next line, i.e. came off maintenance without it being recorded.
For those the start fallback assumes maintenance lasted **zero days**, when the median gap to the
next line is **16.9 months**.

Assuming maintenance ran until the day before the next line is **circular** in principle (it flags
90.1% of those 81, vs 11.1% under the start fallback). It was adopted anyway because the
**discrimination test cleared it**: prevalence at L2 entry rises 8.8% -> 10.1% while the OS hazard
ratio **holds** (1.32 -> 1.37, p 0.048 -> 0.017). Had those records been false positives the HR would
have been dragged toward 1. It was not, so they behave like genuine refractories.

Note this corrects an earlier working assumption that the flag was "a floor because 43% lack end
dates". That was wrong: the great majority of those records are ongoing maintenance and are correctly
classified.

### 4.6 Rejected

- **Review free-text as a progression source**: zero unique events.
- **Cam's `GetRefractory*_Cam.do` as a runtime dependency**: Windows-path, depends on the network
  Subroutines share, and carries a latent bug (`DPMClinicalRelaps` misspelling silently drops the
  clinical-relapse clause). Ported to repo-owned, Mac-native code instead; Cam's files are reference.
- **The MRDR dose field** for the treatment/maintenance dose split: unreliable; form membership is
  used instead (1.3).

### 4.7 Engine wiring (shipped in v3.0)

> **Status.** This wiring is **in the shipped v3.0 model**: both arms are generated and consumed. It
> was held back at the July 2026 maintenance release because the *generation mix* was wrong, not the
> consumption: simulated maintenance-refractory patients were ~6 years younger than registry ones and
> outnumbered the (correctly penalised) treatment-refractory roughly 3:1. Both causes were then found
> and fixed (the maintenance tail rule replaced by the `LENREFR_MNT` logit, and lenalidomide exposure
> in the 'other' regimen bucket made a probability; see 4.4 and 5(6)), and the wiring was released on
> 11 August 2026. What remains is the too-favourable three-year OS in the refractory group, recorded
> in 5 and in `validation.md`.

Both arms are generated and consumed by the engine: `refr_len_tx_in` from the treatment-line logit
and `refr_len_mnt_in` from `LENREFR_MNT`, the L1 maintenance logit that replaced the withdrawn tail
rule (4.4). The two flags remain separate in the data and are collapsed to `refr_len_in` for the
equations that read them (4.1). The engine files:

| piece | file |
|---|---|
| Generation | `core/outcomes/sim_lenrefr.do`, fired at each line-END OMC in `core/simulation_engine.do` |
| Fitted logit | `LENREFR_TX` in `prep/risk_equations.do` (residual arm; 3.5) |
| Consumption | `refr_len_tx_in` in `L2/L3/L4_TXR` and `OS_L2S..L4E` (`sim_txr.do`, `sim_os.do`) |
| CRN / state / helpers | `rn_lenrefr()` (`rng_slots.do`); `vLenRefr_in` (`mata_setup.do`); `get_lenrefr_*` (`mata_functions.do`) |
| Len-regimen codes | `global LENREFR_regimens` in `analyses/<a>/outcomes/txr_<coeffs>.do` (default "7 31") |

**It is a latched state, not a per-line draw.** `vLenRefr_in` starts 0 (0 at L1 by construction) and
flips 0 to 1 the first time a not-yet-refractory patient on a lenalidomide regimen becomes
refractory - definitionally if `BCR` is SD/PD, else a Bernoulli draw from the residual logit. Once 1
it stays 1. The generation fires at a line's **end**, after that line's OS, so this line's `TXR` and
`OS` read the state from *strictly prior* lines - which is how `refr_len_tx_in` was fitted. This is
why the residual logit is fitted on `refr_len_tx_in == 0` rows only and carries no prior-state
covariate: the engine applies it exactly there (3.5).

**The len-gate is by drawn regimen, not a drug binary.** The fit conditions on `Lenalidomide == 1`;
the engine has no drug field, so it counts a line as lenalidomide iff the drawn regimen is a declared
len code (`LENREFR_regimens`). The `0 = other` bucket is treated as non-len. Declared per analysis
alongside the `TXR` list, so a change of modelled regimens carries the gate with it.

**Adding it to OS is mean-preserving redistribution, and that is the point.** `refr_len_tx_in` is a
worse-prognosis covariate (4.1: treatment-dose refractory median OS 24.7 months, HR 1.62; 3.3). So in
`OS_L2..L4` it pulls refractory patients' survival **down** and, because whole-population OS stays
calibrated, non-refractory patients' survival correspondingly **up**. The population mean is held; the
subgroups are separated. That improves the model's **discrimination** (right survival for the right
subgroup, which is what an ICER on a refractory-targeted therapy needs) without disturbing its
**calibration**. The out-of-sample whole-population OS validates within ~1.5% at 3/5/10 years, and
in-sample the L3 regimen/duration overshoot it was built to fix is gone. The *direction* of the
subgroup split is certain (a positive-hazard covariate); its *magnitude* has since been measured and
is too weak (refractory OS too favourable), because the refractory group it acts on is itself
under-generated - see 5(6) for the diagnosis and the two causes.

---

## 5. Known limitations

1. **Maintenance duration is modelled, and maintenance cost is no longer overstated by 69%.** Section
   7 owns this in full: `L1_MNR` / `L1_MND` are fitted and the engine bills the maintenance actually
   delivered. Two limitations remain, both there: pricing is still the blended `cMNT` because only
   lenalidomide has a PBS maintenance listing (7.4), and later-line maintenance (~15% of maintenance
   months) is still costed nowhere (7.3).
2. **There is no maintenance-refractory generation model.** The tail rule that stood here is
   withdrawn (4.4): its AUC was earned by a registry column the engine cannot compute, and stripped
   of that it under-calls badly at long gaps, reporting 33.7% against a registry 70.4%. The binding
   constraint was selection rather than functional form - a *share* needs an observed gap end, which
   is why 7.4 rebuilt it as a survival duration on the maintenance events, made gap-dependent by
   ln(TFI_L1). That rebuild has since been superseded: `L1_MND` no longer carries a gap covariate at
   all, fits on the whole maintenance population, and the gap-band share metric it was scored against
   has been retired as not comparable between the two sides (5(7), 5(8)).
   `L1_MND` is now built and load-bearing for **cost**; the refractory flag derived from it (duration
   reaching the relapse) is the next step but is not yet wired in.
3. **L5+ has no contrast**: 78 to 85% of patients are already len-refractory, so the covariate is not
   identifiable there and is not included.
4. Figures here are in-sample. The out-of-sample validation is the arbiter for the specification
   (see `validation.md`).
5. **Long maintenance is under-observed, and that now limits validation rather than fitting.**
   `L1_MND` fits on the whole maintenance population, so the fit itself is no longer selected. But
   47% of registry lenalidomide-maintenance patients are still ON maintenance at the data cut, and
   half have no recorded end date, so the registry can say little about long episodes. Lenalidomide
   maintenance only became routine after the 2020 PBS listing, so the patients with the longest
   exposure have the shortest follow-up - a maturity problem that later data cuts will ease and no
   specification can.
6. **The refractory subsystem reproduces about a quarter of true L2 refractoriness, and the
   out-of-sample checks (4.7) now measure why.** Whole-population OS validates, but the two direct
   refractory checks fail: prevalence of `refr_len_tx_in` at line entry is under-produced and the gap
   widens with line (L2 4.6% vs 8.3% observed, L3 13.6 vs 25.2, L4 32.9 vs 56.6, L5 45.2 vs 70.1),
   and OS from L2 by refractory status is well-calibrated for the non-refractory arm but far too
   favourable for the refractory arm (3-year 44% vs 21% observed) - the latter downstream of the
   former (too few, too healthy a refractory group). Two distinct causes, of comparable size:

   (a) **The treatment other-lenalidomide tail.** The engine gates refractoriness on the drawn
   regimen being a modelled len code, but 30 to 52% of registry len exposure at L2-L5 sits in
   regimens outside the per-line menu (VRd at L2, Lena monotherapy, Lena/Dara, Lena/Cyclo, Carf/Lena)
   and falls into `other`, where it cannot be gated. Because len patients at L2-L5 are refractory 67
   to 85% of the time, each missed len line is almost certainly a missed refractory, so a small
   exposure gap produces a large prevalence gap. Adding Rd (7) to the L1/L4 menu closed the single
   largest miss (L2 2.9% -> 4.6%); the remainder is a genuine tail that no per-line regimen addition
   closes. The fix, if a refractory-targeted analysis needs the treatment side complete, is to
   decouple the len gate from the modelled-regimen menu - draw len exposure from a registry
   `P(len | line)` - at a cost in statistical coherence (the drawn exposure is uncorrelated with the
   simulated regimen and its response).

   (b) **The maintenance half was not modelled.** *Since fixed - `LENREFR_MNT` now generates it (4.4).
   The quantification below is what motivated that, and the prevalence figures still stand as the
   target.* Refractoriness acquired on L1 lenalidomide MAINTENANCE (`refr_len_mnt_in`) was absent
   from the engine, and it is not a minor add-on: at L2 entry it is 7.1% of patients, essentially the
   same size as treatment-dose
   refractoriness (8.1%), so true L2 refractoriness is 15.5% and the engine models only the treatment
   portion. The treatment flag is clean - just 0.2% of L2 patients are both treatment- and
   maintenance-refractory, so the 8.3% benchmark is genuinely treatment-driven and the
   primary-refractory back-flag (1.5) does not contaminate it. This is the first quantification of the
   maintenance gap, and it made `refr_len_mnt_in` the first-order piece of refractory completeness
   rather than a loose end.

   None of this moves the whole-population projection: the redistribution nets out and whole-pop OS
   validates. It bites only for refractory-targeted analyses, where the engine under-represents true
   refractoriness roughly four-fold at L2 (4.6% modelled of 15.5% true).

7. **Maintenance duration was under-billed. Fixed July 2026 by reversing the draw order.** The
   equation was never wrong: the fitted median was correct on both the registry and the simulated
   case-mix. The DRAW was wrong. `MND` and `TFI_L1` were drawn independently, so a large minority of
   patients received a maintenance duration longer than the gap that had to contain it, and
   `process_data.do` shortened them to fit. That fix-up could only ever shorten, and it was removing
   roughly a third of the median.

   `sim_mnd.do` now runs BEFORE `sim_tfi_l1.do`, from a fit that no longer conditions on the gap, and
   the gap is drawn TRUNCATED below at the maintenance already drawn. `calcSurvTime` maps a survivor
   probability to a time and S is decreasing, so `T >= L` is exactly `U <= S(L)`: drawing
   `U' = U * S(L)` satisfies the ordering by construction, consumes the same random number, and
   leaves common-random-number alignment untouched. Nothing is clipped, so nothing is dragged down.
   The `process_data.do` cap is retained as an instrumented safety net and does not fire.

   Out-of-sample validation improved to **86.5%**, the best this model has recorded (`validation.md`).

   **Two residuals, both recorded rather than fixed.** The simulated mean maintenance duration sits
   well above its median, and cost bills the mean while `mnd_l1.csv` scores the median - so the mean
   has never been checked against the registry. And roughly a quarter of maintenance patients now
   receive a gap barely longer than their maintenance, hence no treatment-free tail, where the
   registry's is substantial. Neither is scored by any current benchmark.

   **The specifications rejected on the way**, each of which reintroduced the selection it was meant
   to escape - every quantity worth conditioning on needs an observed L2, and only a quarter of
   maintenance patients have one:

   | Tried | Why it failed |
   |---|---|
   | Share of the window (`betareg`) | Needs an observed gap end |
   | `ln(gap)` covariate | Same, and it restricted the fit to a quarter of the population |
   | Censor-aware gap | For a censored patient the filled gap is their own censoring time; the share pins at 1.0 |
   | Tail reparameterisation | Convincing on complete gaps, reversed sign on the at-risk population |
   | Drop `ln(gap)`, split by regimen | Correct draw, then the clip destroyed it - **worse** than the original |
   | Two-part tail | The long arm needs an observed L2 too; implied p90 of 201 months |

   Working, figures and the full sequence: `scratch/maintenance/notes.md`.


8. **Benchmarks and the model must measure the same quantity on the same patients, and three times
   they did not.** Each presented initially as a model failure and cost real effort before being
   identified:

   - The **share-of-gap** metric needed an observed L2, so the registry side was computed on
     relapsers while the simulated side had a closed gap for everyone. Retired and replaced by a
     Kaplan-Meier median duration, which needs no closed gap.
   - **Thalidomide** is on an 18-month clock on both sides but by different operations: the target is
     CENSORED at 18, the draw is CAPPED at 18. Those agree on the median only while it sits below 18,
     which it does on both sides today. If either drifts above, the check stops being like-for-like.
   - The MND target **censors death**; the model truncates at it, since maintenance cannot be billed
     after death. Measured and refuted as an explanation for the residual - death moves the registry
     median by under half a month, on 2% of patients - but the asymmetry is real.

   A minimum-N floor of 20 now blanks any cell the held-out fold has split too thin to score, after
   an N=17 cell produced six failures read as a model defect (`validation.md`).

   **The rule this leaves**: before chasing a benchmark failure into the model, check that both sides
   measure the same thing on the same patients.

---

## 6. Reproducing

`prep/refractory_diagnostics.do` regenerates the figures in section 3 from `MRDR Long`. The
exploratory one-offs behind the design decisions live in `scratch/refractory/` and are not tracked.

Construction lives in `prep/sub/MRDR/build_refractory.do` and `prep/data_extraction.do`, both
git-ignored under the data-governance rule (they read raw MRDR); section 2 is their specification of
record.

---

## 7. Maintenance duration: a cost-engine defect (fixed)

Uncovered by the refractory work, but a **costing** problem in its own right. `economic_inputs.md`
points here; this section owns it. 7.1-7.3 are the defect and its size; **7.4 is the fix that was
built** (a capped survival duration - the earlier share-of-the-window design was withdrawn); 7.5-7.6
are a rejected alternative and the implementation traps.

### 7.1 The defect

The engine has no maintenance end date separate from the next line's start, so
`core/process_data.do` (L190) bills maintenance across the **entire** L1-to-L2 gap:

```stata
cost_tx_mnt = cMNT * (TFI_L1 * 30.4375 / 28) if MNT == 1
```

Maintenance is not a modelled episode: `MNT` is a binary, and the gap is charged as though the
patient were on maintenance throughout it.

### 7.2 Size (`scratch/maintenance/mtd_form.do`, 1,571 billed patients)

| | median | mean |
|---|---|---|
| Gap billed | 30.4 mo | 35.9 |
| Maintenance delivered | 14.1 mo | 21.3 |
| Overcharge | 5.9 mo | 14.6 |

**61,347 cycles billed against 36,394 delivered: a 69% overstatement** (1.69x). Lenalidomide
maintenance alone: **39%**. The overcharge has two parts:

| Component | Total months | Share |
|---|---|---|
| **TTM** - billed before maintenance starts (median 4.8 mo, hits **every** patient) | 7,110 | 31% |
| **Post-maintenance** - billed after it ends, within the gap | 15,903 | 69% |

The mechanism is visible by cessation reason: excess is small where maintenance ran to progression
(median +4.2 months) and large where it did not (Planned +19.4, Toxicity +21.0). Only **23.3%** of
ceased episodes end for progression; **76.7%** end for planned/toxicity/other and the patient
relapses later.

*An earlier figure of 127% was quoted from the 651 patients with both an observed duration and an
observed `TFI_L1`. That subset is completers-only, so it excludes the long still-ongoing episodes and
overstates the error. 69% is the population figure.*

### 7.3 Blast radius

`cost_tx_mnt` only fires when the starting line is L1 (`if `L' == 1`, `L = $line`, `$line 0`
resolves to 1). So it affects the **`default` full-pathway analysis** and anything costed from
diagnosis, including budget-impact work. It does **not** affect `transport_dvd` or `car_t`, which set
`$line 2`: maintenance is never costed there. Separately, that means **later-line maintenance is
never costed at all** (about 15% of maintenance months).

### 7.4 The fix (built, simple-first)

Maintenance becomes an episode mirroring a treatment line, so the maintenance block matches the
treatment block:

| Treatment | Maintenance |
|---|---|
| `MNT` logit - whether | unchanged |
| `TXR_L1` - which regimen | **`L1_MNR`** (mlogit, len vs thal) -> `MNR_L1` |
| `TXD_L1` - how long | **`L1_MND`** (parametric survival) -> `MND_L1` |

```
MNR_L1      ~ mlogit(len, thal)                                    [L1_MNR]   sim_mnr.do
MND_L1      ~ streg(Age Age2 Male i.ECOGcc i.RISS SCT), lognormal       sim_mnd.do
              fitted PER REGIMEN, pooled across transplant, no gap term
```

`MNR_L1` is drawn first, then `MND_L1`, then `TFI_L1` - and that order is the design.

**Split by REGIMEN, pooled across transplant.** Lenalidomide and thalidomide are different processes
with non-overlapping ancillaries: thalidomide is a fixed course (9% censored, KM quartiles 5.2 / 10.3
/ 12.6 months), lenalidomide runs to progression (47% censored, 6.5 / 24.6 / 74.7). An AFT carries one
ancillary per equation, so no covariate can reconcile them. The two TRANSPLANT arms, by contrast, have
near-identical Kaplan-Meier curves, so `SCT` enters as a covariate and the arms pool. `BCR` drops out
as a consequence - the arms key on different response variables (`i.BCR_SCT` and `i.BCR_L1`) so
neither serves a pooled fit. A real covariate loss, taken knowingly.

**No gap covariate, and the ordering is enforced downstream instead.** An earlier version carried
`ln(TFI_L1)`, which is missing without an observed L2 and so restricted the fit to a quarter of the
maintenance population - and the short-maintenance quarter at that. Removing it uses all 1,028
lenalidomide patients. But removing it ALONE leaves duration and gap independent, and roughly 40% of
patients then draw maintenance longer than their own gap, which `process_data.do` used to clip back.
That clip could only ever shorten and was removing about a third of the median.

So `sim_tfi_l1.do` runs AFTER `sim_mnd.do` and draws the gap **truncated below** at the maintenance
already drawn. `calcSurvTime` maps a survivor probability to a time and S is decreasing, so `T >= L`
is exactly `U <= S(L)`: drawing `U' = U * S(L)` satisfies the ordering by construction, consumes the
same random number, and leaves common-random-number alignment untouched. The `process_data.do` cap
remains as an instrumented safety net and does not fire.

**Thalidomide is censored at 18 months in the fit and capped there in the draw.** 21 of 289 complete
thalidomide episodes have recorded ends beyond 18 months, out to 95, on a drug given as a ~12-month
course and not prescribed in Australia since 2020; they are 7.3% of patients carrying ~29% of all
thalidomide maintenance months. The PBS cannot adjudicate them - the thalidomide listing is
STREAMLINED with no treatment phase, no continuation rule and no duration limit - so this is a
documented clinical judgement, not a measurement. CENSORED rather than excluded: excluding leaves a
truncated sample and an untruncated family fitted to it undershoots by about a quarter.
`generate_benchmarks.do` carries the same `exit()` so both sides of `mnd_l1.csv` measure the same
quantity.

**Distribution.** Log-normal throughout. Six families were compared per group; AIC and tail weight
rank in OPPOSITE orders, so information criteria alone select the specification that breaks the
simulation - the best-AIC candidates for lenalidomide have no finite mean. Log-normal is the
compromise, and the thalidomide ceiling is what contains its tail. Working:
`scratch/maintenance/notes.md`.


**Lenalidomide and thalidomide only.** The fits restrict to `inlist(MNR_L1, 1, 5)`, so bortezomib,
daratumumab and carfilzomib maintenance are excluded from estimation and the engine never produces
an 'other' maintenance regimen - `sim_mnr` assigns every maintenance patient len or thal. This is the
accepted simplification ("do not even worry about other"). It costs little: bortezomib is 5 to 11% of
starts but has no PBS maintenance DPMQ to price separately anyway (MSAG Clinical Practice Guideline,
June 2022), and daratumumab/carfilzomib maintenance is a couple of dozen patients, mostly later-line.
The regimen mix is era-dependent, which is why len+thal covers both windows without a per-analysis
switch:

| Year | lenalidomide | thalidomide | bortezomib |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2019 | 32.5% | 51.6% | 6.3% |
| 2020 | 88.4% | 1.4% | 3.3% |
| 2023 | 92.9% | **0** | 5.1% |
| 2025 | 88.2% | **0** | 5.9% |

Thalidomide was the majority regimen for most of the registry's history and stopped in 2020 (the
lenalidomide PBS listing). In a modern window it simply empties out: the `r(r) == 1` guard in
`risk_equations.do` then assigns every maintenance patient lenalidomide. So `"1 5"` serves the
historical window the out-of-sample validation scores against and the current one alike, with no
switch.

**Regimen-specific pricing is still blocked, so `c_MNT` stays the blend.** Modelling `MNR_L1` was
meant to allow `c_R` / `c_T` in place of the blended `c_MNT` (roughly 67% lenalidomide / 33%
thalidomide - the all-years mix, wrong for any single year). But per the MSAG guideline only
lenalidomide is PBS-reimbursed for maintenance, so there is no maintenance DPMQ to price thalidomide
or bortezomib with, and unlike duration, cost is not transferable across the era swap. The bill
therefore still uses `c_MNT`. See the Costs todo in the programme note. This is the one part of the
maintenance fix that remains genuinely unfinished.

**The refractory flag is now a natural byproduct, and is the next step.** With the duration modelled
and capped, a patient whose maintenance reaches (within 60 days of) their relapse is still on the drug
at progression, i.e. lenalidomide-refractory. That flag is not built in this pass - 4.4 is where the
refractory generation model is decided - but the capped duration is the component it needs, and
deriving it is a one-liner once the duration model validates.

### 7.5 Why full decomposition was rejected

Modelling TTM, then maintenance, then a true TFI as three sequential events raced against OS is the
most faithful representation, but was rejected twice over:

- **The engine's event machinery assumes strict TXD/TFI alternation keyed on parity.**
  `sim_mort.do` curtails `mTXD[OMC/2]` when `mod(OMC,2)==0` and `mTFI[(OMC+1)/2]` otherwise, so
  inserting maintenance as a first-class event re-indexes every downstream column
  (`mTXD`, `mTFI`, `mTNE`, `mTSD`, `mOS`, `mState`) and every `sim_*` file.
- **It risks the aggregate that currently validates.** `TFI_L1` is fitted directly to the observed
  L1-to-L2 timing; a sum of three independently drawn segments makes that aggregate emergent. This
  model has already rejected one such change on out-of-sample grounds (per-response Weibull shape).

TTM is not modelled **as an event**, and that is what the parity argument above requires. It is
carried as two constants keyed on transplant (7.4), which costs the engine nothing and re-indexes
nothing. The original decision to collapse maintenance to a flag was reasonable; the parity structure
is why.

> *Correction.* This section previously read "TTM is therefore not modelled: it does not affect total
> maintenance cost (price x duration), only where within the gap the cost lands". Both halves are now
> wrong. Under a share of the **window** the cost is `share x (TFI_L1 - TTM)`, so TTM enters the
> arithmetic directly. And it determines when maintenance **ends**, which is what 4.4's definitional
> refractory rule keys on - so TTM affects the pathway, not just where a cost lands. What survives is
> the narrow claim: TTM does not need to be a first-class **event** in the parity-keyed skeleton, and
> a constant is not one.

### 7.6 Note for implementation

`MNT` must key off **the gap the episode sits in**, not the episode number. The first maintenance
episode is not necessarily L1 maintenance: of episodes falling **outside** the L1 gap, 37.4% are
daratumumab (later-line maintenance), against 1.6% inside. The existing
`MNT = 1 if Event1==110 & (Event0==11 | Event0==100)` already does this correctly, and `MND_L1` /
`MNR_L1` follow it by taking the overlap with the gap rather than the first episode.

**This trap has already cost two retracted figures**, both from `scratch/_archive/mnt_duration.do`,
which selects on `MLine==1`: the 127% in 7.2 and the 44.8% / 32.1% binding pair in 7.4. It is not
hypothetical.

Not every regimen is affected the same way. Bortezomib maintenance is **95.4% in-gap** (165 of 173
episodes), so it is genuinely L1 maintenance and cannot be excluded as later-line; daratumumab is
the reverse (58 outside against 30 inside). The keying decides which of those two you see.

Two further traps in `data_extraction.do`:

- **The drug binaries are shared with the chemotherapy rows** after the forms are appended, so every
  reference must be guarded on the maintenance start event. Maintenance daratumumab is
  `Daratumumab`; the chemotherapy column is `Daratumamab` (sic, and it is the only one of the two
  that survives the final `keep`). Reading the chemotherapy spelling on maintenance rows yields zero
  daratumumab episodes, which looks plausible rather than broken.
- **Missing is larger than any number in Stata, and `min()` / `max()` ignore missing arguments.** The
  overlap must be guarded on the episode existing, or `max(., DateL1E)` returns `DateL1E` and a
  patient with one episode is credited with the entire gap three more times.
